title: Preterm Labor
keywords: magnesium 4-6 g load 1-2 g/hr < 32 weeks neuroprotection BEAM
sources: Critical Vector — OB Pocket Guide: Preterm Labor (ACOG 2023)
ACOG Practice Bulletins on preterm labor and antenatal corticosteroid therapy; BEAM trial (Rouse 2008)

changelog.change: Initial entry — diagnosis, the intervention-by-gestational-age table (steroids, magnesium neuroprotection, tocolysis, GBS, progesterone).

summary: The tocolytic buys 48 hours — its only job is to let a course of antenatal steroids take effect and allow transfer to a centre with a NICU. Give magnesium for fetal neuroprotection below 32 weeks. There is no role for maintenance tocolysis.

items: Regular uterine contractions (≥ 4 in 20 min, or ≥ 8 in 1 h), PLUS
Cervical change: ≥ 80% effacement OR dilation > 1 cm; OR a cervical length < 20 mm on transvaginal ultrasound.
Fetal fibronectin has a high negative predictive value — a negative test with a cervical length 20–30 mm makes preterm delivery within 7–14 days unlikely.

rows: 12 mg IM q24h ×2. A single rescue course if > 14 days since the first and delivery is again likely before 34 wk. (Dexamethasone 6 mg IM q12h ×4 is an alternative.)
4–6 g IV load, then 1–2 g/h. Reduces cerebral palsy (BEAM). Continue until delivery or ~12–24 h
Goal is the steroid window. Nifedipine first-line; indomethacin < 32 wk (watch ductal constriction / oligohydramnios if > 48 h). NO maintenance tocolysis
Treat as GBS-positive if status unknown and < 37 wk — penicillin G (cefazolin if low-risk penicillin allergy; clindamycin only if susceptible / vancomycin otherwise)
16–36 wk, singleton + prior spontaneous preterm birth
Vaginal progesterone 200 mg nightly if a short cervix; 17-OHP caproate 250 mg IM weekly (note the reduced regulatory support after the PROLONG trial)

body.text: Rule out and treat the drivers: intra-amniotic infection (fever, uterine tenderness, fetal tachycardia → deliver, do not tocolyse), abruption, and preterm prelabour rupture of membranes. Do not tocolyse against non-reassuring fetal status, significant bleeding, severe preeclampsia, or chorioamnionitis.
